questions.q: What does a row access policy control, as opposed to a masking policy?
options: Whether an entire row is visible to the querying role, not what a column's value looks like
Which warehouse a query runs on
How long a query is allowed to run
Which database a role can connect to
questions.explain: A row access policy is a boolean expression: TRUE means the row is visible, FALSE means it's silently filtered out. Masking policies, by contrast, change what a visible row's column values look like.

questions.q: Why does the lesson use a mapping table (governance.row_policy_map) instead of hardcoding role names into the row access policy itself?
options: Mapping tables run faster than any other approach
Hardcoded role names are not allowed in Snowflake SQL
A mapping table scales — granting a new role access is an INSERT, not a rewrite of the policy object
Mapping tables are required by Snowflake for all row access policies
questions.explain: With the mapping-table pattern, adding a new role's access is a simple INSERT into a real table. Hardcoding role names directly into the policy would require editing and redeploying the policy object itself for every new role.

questions.q: What happens to a row when a row access policy's boolean expression evaluates to FALSE for the current role?
options: The query throws a permissions error
The row is returned with all columns NULL
The row is silently excluded from the result set, with no error or indication
The entire query fails
questions.explain: A row access policy filters rows silently — FALSE means the row just isn't in the result, with no error raised.

questions.q: In the Tokyo screenshot, the FIRST_NAME and LAST_NAME columns are also masked. What does this demonstrate?
options: Row access policies automatically mask columns too
The screenshot is from a different, unrelated table
Row access policies and masking policies are mutually exclusive — only one can be active per table
Row access policies and masking policies are independent mechanisms that can stack on the same table simultaneously
questions.explain: The table has both a row access policy (filtering which rows show up) and masking policies (filtering what visible rows' values look like) active at once — they're independent and stack without conflict.

questions.q: What does ALTER TABLE raw_customer.customer_loyalty ADD ROW ACCESS POLICY ... ON (city) actually do?
options: Creates a brand-new row access policy object
Attaches an already-created row access policy to the table, naming which column its signature maps to
Deletes all existing rows where city is NULL
Grants the PUBLIC role access to the table
questions.explain: ALTER TABLE ... ADD ROW ACCESS POLICY ... ON (city) attaches a previously created policy object to the table, specifying which column (city) the policy's signature argument maps to.
